title: Apply dynamic HDR encode policy routing
summary: Apply the existing Dynamic HDR encode preservation decision to Do-Encode before FFmpeg attempt planning. Preserve/review routes now fail closed to operator review, preserve/remux routes try a guarded remux fallback before allowing warn/drop encode behavior, and DynamicHdrPolicy=off skips Dynamic HDR probes.
reason: Dynamic HDR detection, planning, and x265 parameter helpers existed, but the encode route still ignored preserve/remux/review policy decisions at runtime.
behavior_before: Do-Encode detected Dynamic HDR metadata and always warned that encode would drop it, even when DynamicHdrPolicy requested preserve_or_review or preserve_or_remux. DynamicHdrPolicy=off still paid the Dynamic HDR probe cost, and encode-to-remux Dynamic HDR fallback had no dedicated rejection evidence.
behavior_after: Do-Encode skips Dynamic HDR probes when DynamicHdrPolicy=off. Under preserve_or_review, unsupported or not-yet-wired preserve encode decisions register operator_required dynamic-hdr-policy failures before FFmpeg attempt planning. Under preserve_or_remux, Do-Encode tries a guarded Do-Remux fallback; codec-policy rejection records Dynamic HDR remux fallback evidence and then allows warning/drop encode semantics.
tests_added: Expanded Invoke-DynamicHdrDetectionChecks.ps1 static assertions for encode policy routing and guarded remux fallback evidence.
manual_validation: SKIPPED: Representative real-media Dynamic HDR validation remains required before daily-driver completion.
rollback_plan: Revert the encode/remux policy-routing edits and the matching Dynamic HDR detection test assertions.
notes:
Touches FFmpeg/media-policy-adjacent routing. Do not claim full Dynamic HDR preservation until extraction/injection, output verification, and representative real-media validation are complete.
